transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-30
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~52m
Recording id: ff-20250730-8734-rcv
Attendees: Avery Kline (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (LuminaHealth Head of ML), Emily Zhou (LuminaHealth SRE), Ravi Patel (LuminaHealth PM), Sana Ahmed (LuminaHealth Compliance)

-- Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
Redwood and LuminaHealth aligned on POC acceptance gates: latency p95 target, throughput target, functional accuracy thresholds, cost guardrails, reporting format (CSV + JSON summary), and runbook for benchmark execution. Agreed owners and due dates for artifacts. Next: Redwood to share final acceptance matrix and runbook; kickoff benchmark the week of Aug 4.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: ok hey everyone thanks for making the time, this is the success gates and runbook signoff for the POC, our goal is to lock thresholds and reporting so the benchmark is unambiguous.
[00:18] Carlos: yeah hi thanks, should be under an hour i hope. We mostly want to validate performance against our prod-like traffi—traffic pattern and make sure quality doesn't regress.
[00:29] Priya: great, quick agenda: 1) confirm workload sizing (sequence lengths, qps/peak), 2) acceptance metrics (latency p95, error budget, quality), 3) benchmark procedure and artifacts, 4) reporting template and signoff.
[00:45] Emily: i'll jump in on traffic - we can provide traces from last 30 days, average concurrency is around 120 simultaneous requests, baseline qps ~90, peak bursts up to 420 for 30-90s. Typical prompt length average token length 128, 95th ~480 tokens.
[01:05] Ravi: and on accuracy we care about two things: first, the NLU intent classification F1 shouldn't drop more than 1.5 points compared to current model; second, generated responses' hallucination rate measured by the eval set should be <4%.
[01:22] Priya: ok sounds reasonable. For the latency SLOs what are you aiming for? p95, p99?
[01:28] Carlos: p95 is primary — we need <350ms for interactive experiences. p99 under 700ms is desirable but higher tolerance.
[01:38] Marta: i'll note a practical acceptance: p95 <=350ms on the synthetic workload that mirrors your traces, with <1% error rate (5xxs, timeouts) and throughput sustain at 90 qps baseline and ability to absorb 420 qps bursts with graceful degradation.
[01:55] Carlos: yep and cost — we have a cost ceiling for this POC of roughly $X per 10k requests? we need a rule of thumb.
[02:03] Avery: we can provide estimated unit economics post-benchmark. For acceptance we recommend a soft cost guardrail: incremental inference cost not exceed $0.002 per token on average for the tested config — if cost is higher we will propose quantization/ batching adjustments and a rerun.
[02:25] Emily: re: security/compliance, we need to confirm KMS integration and audit logs during POC, not just after. Sana can you remind the team?
[02:33] Sana: yes KMS & audit logs are must-haves. We also need to confirm that logs can be redacted and that no raw PII is stored in long-term telemetry. That will be a gating item.
[02:45] Priya: noted — we'll include explicit checks in the runbook: verify KMS calls, ensure redact rules on logs, and a sample of audit events.
[02:55] Jordan: also one operational ask — define rollback triggers. If during the benchmark we see sustained p95 > 600ms or error rate >5%, we want automated fallback to a lower-cost regional pool or model variant.
[03:10] Marta: agreed, we will include a fallback policy example and an automatic failover step in the runbook.
[03:18] Carlos: sounds good. Now, reporting — what format do you typically deliver? we want something machine-readable to feed into our dashboard.
[03:27] Avery: we'll provide a two-part deliverable: 1) CSV with per-run time-series: timestamp, run_id, qps, concurrency, avg_latency_ms, p50,p90,p95,p99, error_count, tokens_generated, cost_usd; 2) JSON summary with aggregated metrics and pass/fail flags and a short human-readable PDF/slide summary. We'll also attach raw logs (redacted) and the harness config.
[03:53] Ravi: ok can you include evaluation metrics like F1 and hallucination % per checkpoint?
[03:58] Priya: yes, the CSV will include extra columns for quality metrics: eval_f1, hallucination_pct, rouge_l (if applicable).
[04:08] Carlos: what about the acceptance logic — is it simple AND or a weighted score?
[04:15] Marta: propose a deterministic gate set: pass if ALL primary gates met: (a) p95 <=350ms, (b) error_rate <1%, (c) eval_f1 drop <=1.5 pts, (d) hallucination_pct <4%, (e) cost_per_token <=0.002. If any primary gate fails, we mark as go/no-go = NO and list remediation steps. Secondary gates (p99, peak burst behavior) are advisory and if they fail we'll call for follow-up tuning and possible re-run.
[04:46] Emily: that deterministic approach is good for procurement and signoff.
[04:51] Carlos: agreed. One question: how will you measure hallucination % reliably? we have a labeled eval set but it's not huge.
[04:58] Priya: for this POC we'll use your labeled eval set as the source of truth; we'll also sample 200 free-form responses from the system during the synthetic load and run them through the same annotation pipeline. Annotation noise acknowledged but we'll include confidence intervals in the report.
[05:15] Ravi: timeline? when do you want to run the benchmark?
[05:19] Avery: proposing week of Aug 4 for the first run. Prep work (artifact exchange, traces, infra) to complete by Aug 1. Then a 2-day benchmark window and 24-48h for Redwood to analyze and deliver the report.
[05:32] Carlos: that works. We can turn around traces + eval set by Aug 1.
[05:36] Sana: and compliance will need the SOC2 answer set by Aug 5.
[05:40] Marta: we'll send SOC2 & KMS integration notes by Aug 5.
[05:46] Priya: ok, let's walk through the benchmark steps in the runbook — i'll narrate and you can interrupt. Step 0: pre-checks — ensure KMS configured, audit events enabled, test account keys exchanged.
[05:58] Priya: Step 1: deploy benchmark harness in Redwood test environment with the same model artifact you plan to use. We'll pin model version to avoid drift.
[06:06] Priya: Step 2: replayer — feed your production traces into harness with time-scaling to reproduce bursts. We'll run three phases: baseline (30 min at 90 qps), stress (15 min ramp to 420 qps), and soak (60 min at average qps). Each run will capture full latency distributions and server-side metrics.
[06:27] Carlos: soak of 60 min is a lot; can we do 30? we want to keep infra costs cap.
[06:32] Priya: yes we can reduce soak to 30 min for the POC; for full validation we'd prefer 60 but understand cost constraints. We'll make that adjustable in the runbook.
[06:40] Marta: Step 3: quality eval — run eval checkpoints during baseline and stress phases, collect sample responses and compute eval_f1 and hallucination metrics.
[06:49] Priya: Step 4: cost accounting — we'll record token counts per run and map to cost model; we'll compute cost_per_token and projected monthly runrate.
[06:58] Emily: please include exact columns for CSV so we can ingest directly.
[07:02] Avery: will do — sample column list will be attached to the template: run_id, phase, timestamp, qps, concurrency, avg_latency_ms, p50_ms, p90_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, error_count, tokens_generated, cost_usd, eval_f1, hallucination_pct.
[07:20] Carlos: and for pass/fail a single summarized field?
[07:23] Marta: JSON summary will include boolean pass_primary_gates, list failed_gates, notes, and per-gate measured_value and threshold.
[07:33] Ravi: ok tell me about reruns — if we fail a gate what's the cadence for remediation and re-test?
[07:38] Avery: standard POC flow: one remediation cycle included — we'll propose tuning (quantization, batching, different model variant, routing) and run one re-test within 10 business days. Additional re-tests are subject to new agreement.
[07:50] Carlos: good. Also want to have a human signoff event after report delivery — procurement needs an email acceptance.
[07:57] Jordan: we'll include a signoff page in the final PDF that both parties can sign/confirm via email.
[08:05] Sana: small note — wherever logs or traces are shared we need a data processing agreement addendum. Not a blocker but important.
[08:12] Avery: understood, we'll loop legal if needed.
[08:15] Priya: any other technical constraints? e.g., private deployment or VPC?
[08:20] Carlos: for the POC we prefer Redwood Hosted with a dedicated tenant. If things look promising we'll discuss private deployment later. For now hosted dedicated pool is fine.
[08:30] Marta: we'll run the benchmark in the dedicated pool that mirrors production capacity. We'll also record region and NVidia/AMP hardware details in the report.
[08:38] Emily: about observability: we want trace-level metrics exported to our tracing endpoint; is that supported for the POC?
[08:44] Priya: yes we can export limited traces; we will redact PII and provide sampling config.
[08:49] Carlos: ok great. Anything else?
[08:52] Ravi: one last ask — can you include a simple acceptance checklist in the runbook so our procurement folks can verify quickly?
[08:59] Avery: yes — checklist will mirror the primary gates plus docs delivered (SOC2, KMS notes, runbook, CSV/JSON report, signed acceptance).
[09:08] Carlos: perfect. Let's recap owners and dates.
[09:12] Avery: recap: Redwood sends acceptance matrix + CSV/JSON template (Avery) by 2025-08-01; Redwood to prepare benchmark harness and schedule kickoff (Priya) week of 2025-08-04; LuminaHealth to share traces + eval set (Carlos/Emily) by 2025-08-01; SOC2/KMS notes (Marta/Sana) by 2025-08-05; one test run during Aug 4-8 window, report back within 48h of run.
[09:40] Carlos: confirmed, we'll sign off after review and get procurement engaged.
[09:45] Avery: thanks all — i'll send the doc and a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.
[09:50] Emily: thanks everyone.
[09:52] End meeting.

Attachments referenced: acceptance-matrix-template.csv (to be attached), benchmark-harness-config.yaml (to be attached), SOC2-summary.pdf (link to be shared), sample-run-report.json (example).

Explicit go/no-go thresholds (as recorded):
- Latency: p95 <= 350 ms (primary)
- Errors: error_rate (5xx/timeouts) < 1% (primary)
- Quality: eval_f1 drop <= 1.5 points vs baseline (primary)
- Hallucination: < 4% measured on eval and sampled responses (primary)
- Cost: cost_per_token <= $0.002 (primary)
- Peak/burst: able to absorb 420 qps bursts with graceful degradation; p99 <= 700ms (secondary)

Report columns (CSV): run_id, phase, timestamp, qps, concurrency, avg_latency_ms, p50_ms, p90_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, error_count, tokens_generated, cost_usd, eval_f1, hallucination_pct

Runbook highlights:
- Pre-checks: KMS, audit logs, redaction rules, keys exchanged
- Deployment: pinned model artifact, run in dedicated pool
- Phases: baseline (30m at 90 qps), stress (15m ramp to 420 qps), soak (30m at average qps)
- Quality evals: checkpoints during baseline & stress + 200 free-form samples
- Cost calc: token accounting mapped to cost per token and projected monthly run costs
- Fallback: automatic regional model variant failover if sustained p95 > 600ms or error_rate > 5%

Final note: Customer acceptance requires the primary gates to pass and an emailed signoff. If any primary gate fails Redwood will provide remediation recommendations and one re-test within 10 business days.
